what: NUCLEO-F429ZI lwIP httpd + altcp_tls + mbedTLS, make ROMTABLES=1, the first 50 000 exchanges of a 250 000-exchange single TLS session, 2026-10-09

victim.stack: lwIP httpd over lwIP altcp_tls on mbedTLS, all three out of STM32CubeF4, built as they ship
victim.table: mbedTLS FSb, 256 x 1 byte (the 4-table build's final-round S-box)

geometry.note: 0x0801e944 is 4 bytes into its 16-byte flash row. A different number from the SNMPv3 victim's 12 even though both are mbedTLS FSb, because -fdata-sections makes the linker's ordering depend on everything else in the image. Measured both ways on this capture, vote only, in exchanges: at offset 4 the vote is 4/8/14/15/15 of 16 at 12.5k/25k/50k/100k/150k, at offset 0 it is 0/0/2/14. So the right offset is worth about a factor of two in exchanges here.

attack.expect_note: record key recovered and verified; the vote reaches 14/16 and the free (P^IV, C_1) pair settles the remaining two by sweeping all 120 byte pairs
attack.note: n is null, so every conditioned exchange in the vector is used - about 40 000 of the 50 000, since `mode` conditioning drops the rest. Each exchange carries 15 AES blocks and the blocks are the traces, so that is around 600 000 traces from 40 000 measured turnarounds.

truth.note: the TLS 1.2 server write key for that one session, which is what the attack recovers - not a long-lived secret. It is in the vector so the packer can check E(K, P^C_prev) == C before writing. The recovery uses the free known pair instead and needs no key, which is also why the demo can be checked by anyone holding the capture.
